problem_text:
A manufacturing network aims to devise a quality improvement strategy to lower total defect rates arising from several production lines. Initially, no corrective procedures are in place.

The operational characteristics for each production line are as follows:
* For Line 1, defect coefficient is 1.945, throughput is 141.89.
* For Line 2, defect coefficient is 1.032, throughput is 240.651.
* For Line 3, defect coefficient is 2.142, throughput is 193.525.
* For Line 4, defect coefficient is 1.061, throughput is 251.805.
* For Line 5, defect coefficient is 0.771, throughput is 261.289.
* For Line 6, defect coefficient is 2.613, throughput is 293.637.

To address defects, several corrective protocols are available, each with a specific defect reduction rate:
* By implementing Protocol A, defects will be lowered by 24%.
* By implementing Protocol B, defects will be lowered by 41%.
* By implementing Protocol C, defects will be lowered by 39%.
* By implementing Protocol D, defects will be lowered by 88%.
* By implementing Protocol E, defects will be lowered by 16%.
* By implementing Protocol F, defects will be lowered by 24%.

Applying a corrective protocol to a production line incurs an incremental cost per unit of throughput. The cost matrix for all line–protocol combinations is detailed below:

| Line \ Protocol | Protocol A | Protocol B | Protocol C | Protocol D | Protocol E | Protocol F |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|
| Line 1 | 60.815 | 44.279 | 143.513 | 68.707 | 74.567 | 11.16 |
| Line 2 | 175.274 | 117.601 | 86.149 | 36.956 | 130.303 | 15.825 |
| Line 3 | 151.761 | 50.875 | 89.768 | 74.77 | 80.31 | 147.103 |
| Line 4 | 157.599 | 117.843 | 26.142 | 19.996 | 39.908 | 127.389 |
| Line 5 | 138.054 | 61.7 | 135.768 | 102.276 | 93.988 | 61.902 |
| Line 6 | 153.439 | 31.625 | 91.684 | 63.817 | 138.912 | 102.46 |

Determine how to assign corrective protocols to each production line (lines may employ multiple protocols concurrently), and note that a line may also operate with partial correction if needed. The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate defect quantity is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.534 of the baseline amount, while minimizing the total incremental expenditure.
